clue.text: Watch record being made — what a hero's welcome!

parts.note: ticker is slang for a watch, from its ticking
a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: A watch's record is being made: what a welcome for a hero!
explanation.walkthrough: A hero returning to New York is greeted with a shower of paper streamers thrown from office windows.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrated people are honoured with a parade under streams of thrown paper strips, so this is what such a welcome consists of.

clue.text: Quarrel when man of action loses plane, say?

indicators.note: loses means a part of the longer word is dropped

parts.note: a plaintiff is one who brings a legal action

indicators.note: say means plane is spoken, giving a word of the same sound but different spelling

parts.note: plane is said here, to be heard as a homophone meaning flat or simple

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out when a man of action loses his aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man of action' suggests a hero but is the person bringing a lawsuit; 'say' turns plane into PLAIN, which 'loses' takes off the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty argument or squabble, a synonym.

clue.text: Gambling stake in many a joint

definitions.text: Gambling stake in many a joint

parts.words: Gambling stake in many a joint
parts.note: a counter used as a bet in a gambling joint, where it is also on the plate in many a cafe

explanation.surface: Wagers placed in seedy gambling dens.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid as held prints CHID, a misread of the final letter; the clue plainly gives the gaming counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plastic counter stands for money when betting in a casino.

clue.text: Transitoriness of one theme player composed

indicators.note: composed suggests music written out, so the letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A player composing a short-lived theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' shuffles I, THEME and PLAYER together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral things last only a day or so, so this means fleetingness.

clue.text: A little bit of contact

explanation.surface: A slight physical brush.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight amount, as in a trace of salt; and physical contact as when hands meet.

clue.text: Openly worried about the plastic wrapping

indicators.note: about places the shuffled letters around the little word
worried means agitated, so the letters of openly are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone openly fretting over the plastic packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Openly' looks like an adverb on 'worried', but it is the fodder; 'worried' reworks it and 'about' wraps that round the little word.
explanation.definitionFit: A common plastic, made into thin sheets and bags for packaging food and goods.

clue.text: Prospect for half a dozen bridge partners

parts.note: six, written as the Roman numeral VI
East and West are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A view on who might make six bridge partners.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named after compass points, and East and West play together.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a scene or outlook seen from a place, a synonym.

clue.text: Unlucky having taken leading part after bad opening

indicators.note: after places the actor's word following the word for bad

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will
an actor who starred took the leading role

explanation.surface: Unlucky actor who got the lead after a disastrous first night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' suggests a play's first night, but it only tells us the piece for 'bad' opens the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being born under an evil star means being doomed or ill-fated.

clue.text: Itching feet? For poor Andrew a deadly sin

indicators.note: poor shows the letters of the name are in a sorry, mixed-up state

parts.note: lust is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Poor Andrew's restless feet are a deadly sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' shuffles ANDREW into WANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchy feet is an idiom for a strong urge to travel and roam.

clue.text: Last word from our correspondent even if not a Muslim?

definitions.meaning: true to one's faith, as a believer of any religion is

explanation.surface: How a letter-writer signs off, whatever their religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal letter closes with 'Yours' and this adverb; and a devout believer of any creed acts in this loyal, believing way.

clue.text: Rejected North Mountain project

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the two pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: A scheme for the north mountain has been turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns NALP round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A project is a scheme or intended course of action, a synonym.

clue.text: Bit of chicken should be good for a giggle?

definitions.meaning: the forked breastbone of a fowl

definitions.text: should be good for a giggle?
definitions.meaning: a jolly notion, a cheerful idea

explanation.surface: Some chicken that should be good for a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: The wishbone of a bird, pulled for luck; and read as two words, a jolly idea.

clue.text: The pie Martha cooked in dramatic setting

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are doctored and reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Martha's pie is baked in a theatrical venue.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-air arena with tiered seats is a classical place for staging plays and spectacles.

clue.text: Transport being train to carry all the world?

parts.note: Shakespeare's 'All the world's a stage', from As You Like It
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: A train able to carry everyone on earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' and 'to carry' only link: the coach carries the stage, as the old vehicle ran stage by stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-drawn vehicle that carried passengers on regular routes is a form of transport.

clue.text: Being partial to about a pound of vanilla perhaps

indicators.note: about means the longer word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: favouring means being partial to or preferring
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone who likes roughly a pound of vanilla.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vanilla perhaps' is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is one example of a substance added to food to give it taste.

clue.text: New role in the board is not too bad

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for the board

parts.note: a board is a table, as in 'board and lodging'

indicators.note: new indicates the letters of role are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new role on the board of directors isn't too bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' suggests directors, but it is the table, as in 'board and lodging'; 'New' reshuffles the role and 'in' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bearable or passable is fair enough, without being good, a synonym.

clue.text: Repairing robot I err — should pipe come from here?

indicators.note: repairing means fixing, so the letters are rebuilt in a different order

explanation.surface: A robot admits its mistake while being mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repairing' shuffles ROBOT I ERR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobacco pipes are carved from the woody root of the heath plant, so a pipe comes from there.

clue.text: Capek's work; by a student of the country

parts.note: R.U.R. is the 1920 play by Karel Capek that introduced the word robot
L is the learner or student, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A note on a Capek work beside a student's name.
explanation.walkthrough: R.U.R. is Karel Capek's Czech play about robots; L stands for learner, the letter on a British learner driver's plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes countryside places and life, as opposed to the town.

clue.text: Whereby lots of things get knocked down

definitions.text: Whereby lots of things get knocked down

parts.words: Whereby lots of things get knocked down
parts.note: reads like demolition, but lots are items in an auction and 'knocked down' means sold with a tap of a hammer

explanation.surface: Describing a wrecking ball that topples many buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: An auctioneer's small hammer is tapped to mark each lot as sold.

clue.text: Lack of motive power when one 13 enters, tipsily, in opposite directions

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the pair of compass points

parts.note: North and South are opposite compass points

indicators.note: tipsily means drunkenly, so the letters of enters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lacking get-up-and-go wanders in, drunk, in both directions at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposite directions' gives two compass points, North and South; 'tipsily' staggers the letters of 'enters' and 'in' places them between those two.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia in a body is its inability to move itself, so inertness is having no motive power.

clue.text: Bar course for a singer

parts.note: a bar in a pub is the counter
tenor means a course or general direction, as in 'the tenor of his life'

explanation.surface: A bar's course, as if a pub meal were on offer to a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A male alto voice is a type of singer, the highest adult male voice.

clue.text: Jane imprisons one mountain stronghold

indicators.note: imprisons means the name locks the numeral inside itself

parts.note: Jane Eyre is Charlotte Bronte's heroine
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Jane locks someone up in a mountain fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'one in a mountain stronghold'; those extra words only link. Jane Eyre is the heroine of Charlotte Bronte's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest built high on a crag, used figuratively for a lofty fortress.

clue.text: Ruin, and for some Europeans nothing more

indicators.note: more means the next piece is added on after

parts.note: und is German for 'and'
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Ruin, and for some Europeans nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some Europeans' are German speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo something is to bring it to ruin, as in 'his greed undid him'.

clue.text: Overhead cover for puss, say

indicators.note: say means the word for puss is spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: puss is an old country name for a hare

explanation.surface: Something to cover a cat's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puss' looks like a cat, but is a traditional name for a hare.
explanation.definitionFit: What grows on the head covers the top of us, a whimsical definition.

clue.text: Related to a top man on board, almost

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: the king is the most important piece on a chessboard

explanation.surface: Kin to a captain or other leading figure on a ship's board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' is a chessboard, where the king is the key piece; 'almost' drops the G of KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of the same family or similar character means being connected or kindred.

clue.text: Madly ordering a hundred mistakes to be rectified

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: madly means the letters go wild and end in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone frantically ordering a hundred errors to be put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madly' shuffles ORDERING plus A; C comes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin plural names errors in a printed book listed for correction, like errata.

clue.text: Boy's colour is sound

definitions.note: read as 'Boy is', the definition is just the boy's name

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for colour is only said, its spelling then changed

parts.note: hue is a colour or tint

explanation.surface: A boy's colour is fine, sound and healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is sound' looks like a verdict that the colour is healthy; really 'sound' means said out loud, and 'Boy's' is 'Boy is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name; Hugh is a common male first name.

clue.text: An. out-of-the-way entrance

parts.note: seems to mean a remote, hidden door, but read literally it is a door leading out to the way, the public road

explanation.surface: A secluded, hard-to-find doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The stop after 'An' is a printing mark on the page and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: The front door of a house opening directly onto the public road.
